fixes.explanation: That's it, baker. The angel "…placed his right foot on the sea and his left foot on the land." (Revelation 10:2) One foot in the water, one foot on the ground, and a little scroll lying open in his hand. I stay put on my gold base, and I still wobble when the floor gets sticky.

A mountain and a valley sound like a fine place to stand, friend. But the text doesn't mention either one. It says he placed his right foot on the sea and his left foot on the land (Revelation 10:2). One foot on the sea, one on the land, and I think my back would file a complaint.

Good guess, friend, since the thunders were just in the scene. But the thunders' words were sealed, and the angel doesn't say they'll speak again. What he swears is, “There will be no more delay!” (Revelation 10:6) Then he says the mystery of God will be fulfilled when the seventh angel begins to sound his trumpet (Revelation 10:7).

That one isn't what the angel says here, friend. He says that in the days of the seventh angel, “…the mystery of God will be fulfilled…” (Revelation 10:7) That's the one thing he names as getting fulfilled.

Good try, baker, because Revelation does talk about a harvest elsewhere (Revelation 14:15–16). But this angel says something different. When the seventh angel begins to sound his trumpet, “…the mystery of God will be fulfilled…” (Revelation 10:7) I'd stick to what he actually says, like I stick to the recipe.

The elders are in Revelation, baker (Revelation 4:4), but not in this verse. The angel says it will be fulfilled “…just as He proclaimed to His servants the prophets.” (Revelation 10:7) The prophets are the ones who got the word.

You've got it, baker. The voice says, “Go, take the small scroll that lies open in the hand of the angel standing on the sea and on the land.” (Revelation 10:8) That's a mighty angel to walk up to. I'd be rehearsing my "excuse me" the whole way over.

Sealed servants do show up in Revelation, baker (Revelation 7:3–4). But nobody asks John to count them here. The voice tells him, “Go, take the small scroll that lies open in the hand of the angel standing on the sea and on the land.” (Revelation 10:8)

That's right, baker. John says he ate it, “…and it was as sweet as honey in my mouth. But when I had eaten it, my stomach turned bitter.” (Revelation 10:10) Same two things the angel told him (Revelation 10:9), just in the order John felt them. Nothing came out different.
